title: What gives impact
header_line: My analysis of one book on an entrepreneur's life. Not a summary of the book. Not affiliated with or endorsed by the author or publisher.

lines.text: What have you heard on a call like this that only later turned out to change you?

I said there are things in what we discuss that will give us a lot of impact. It is difficult to notice what gives us impact: you heard something that called your attention, and maybe three or four months later you notice it was a catalyst for you becoming a certain way.

It can be sudden, it can happen over a period of time, it can be surprising, I said. It's not the amount of communication or content. It's about grasping the impact these concepts have on us. My goal is for us to collaborate so these concepts have major impact in our lives.

I said that in this chapter we see again good displays of the person's leadership. A student said: he wanted to make sure he was doing something different. They chose an outer frame of steel instead of pinning things down to a frame from the inside.

I want to come out and make a confession, I said. His leadership style is interesting to me because he focuses on experimentation, on pushing the limits, on ambition. He has tremendous agility. Even when people disagree he has intuition and pushes the limits.

I said to a student who works on their own: you can look up and call me, and I can offer you feedback and what I would do. But in the end, what am I doing as a leader? Am I teaching you to find solutions, or am I finding the solutions for you?
What has changed in you in the last few months, and which call changed it?

exercise.title: Five minutes
steps: Write one idea from these classes that changed something for you months later.
Write the style of leadership you most admire in the book, in one line.
Write whether you teach people to find solutions or find them for them.
Write how you will notice the impact in three months.

check.q: What did I say about noticing impact?
choices: You may notice it months later

check.q: What did I say the person's leadership focuses on?
What question did I ask myself as a leader?
choices: Am I teaching you to find solutions or finding them for you?

recap: Notice what changes you, even months later. Teach people to find solutions.
